children: US energy firms likely added a below-normal 79 billion cubic feet of natural gas into storage last week, according to the average estimate in a Reuters poll released on Wednesday.
The estimate compares with an injection of 77 bcf during the same week a year ago and an average increase for that week of 96 bcf over the past five years (2021 to 2025).
In the prior week ended September 25, energy firms added 64 bcf of gas into storage. (USOILN=ECI)

If correct, the forecast for the week ended October 2 would increase stockpiles to 3.494 trillion cubic feet. That would be about 3.7% below the same week a year ago and about 1.8% above the five-year average for the week.
The US Energy Information Administration is scheduled to release its weekly storage report at 10:30 a.m. EDT (1430 GMT) on Thursday.
There were 63 total degree days (TDDs) last week, matching the 30-year normal of 63 TDDs for the period, data from financial firm LSEG showed.
Total degree days measure the number of degrees a day's average temperature is above or below 65 degrees Fahrenheit (18 degrees Celsius) to estimate demand to cool or heat homes and businesses.
Reuters polled 10 analysts, whose estimates ranged from injections of 74 bcf to 86 bcf, with a median increase of 79 bcf.
Early estimates for the week ending October 9 showed an average increase of 77 bcf.
That figure compares with an injection of 80 bcf during the same week last year and a five-year average increase of 90 bcf.
